# MA322 Quiz 3 Review Answers

**1.** Suppose we have a product with price (low, high), brand (Levis, Lees), and cut (Boot, Regular). The levels are coded 0, 1 in the order listed: price low = 0, high = 1; brand Levis = 0, Lees = 1; cut Boot = 0, Regular = 1.

We have 3 customers, and a regression for each customer on this product gives the coefficients below. Evaluate 2 new products for these customers, then find the overall preferences for the two products.

**New Product Analysis**

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Profile} & \textbf{Price} & \textbf{Brand} & \textbf{Cut} \\ \hline
Product 1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ \hline
Product 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{=html}
<table style="border-collapse: collapse; margin: 1em auto; text-align: center;">
<tr><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Profile</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Price</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Brand</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Cut</th></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Product 1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">0</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Product 2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">0</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td></tr>
</table>
```
:::

**Regression Coefficients**

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
 & \textbf{Customer 1} & \textbf{Customer 2} & \textbf{Customer 3} \\ \hline
Price & $-2$ & 1 & 2 \\ \hline
Brand & $-3$ & 2 & $-1$ \\ \hline
Cut & 1 & $-2$ & 3 \\ \hline
Intercept & 8 & 5 & 4 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{=html}
<table style="border-collapse: collapse; margin: 1em auto; text-align: center;">
<tr><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;"></th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Customer 1</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Customer 2</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Customer 3</th></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Price</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">−2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">2</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Brand</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">−3</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">−1</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Cut</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">−2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">3</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 6px 14px;">Intercept</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">8</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">5</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">4</td></tr>
</table>
```
:::

Predicted rating = Intercept + Price coef $\times$ price + Brand coef $\times$ brand + Cut coef $\times$ cut.

Customer 1: Product 1 = $8 + (-2)(1) + (-3)(1) + (1)(0) = 3$; Product 2 = $8 + (-2)(0) + (-3)(1) + (1)(1) = 6$ \
Customer 2: Product 1 = $5 + (1)(1) + (2)(1) + (-2)(0) = 8$; Product 2 = $5 + (1)(0) + (2)(1) + (-2)(1) = 5$ \
Customer 3: Product 1 = $4 + (2)(1) + (-1)(1) + (3)(0) = 5$; Product 2 = $4 + (2)(0) + (-1)(1) + (3)(1) = 6$

a) Fill in the predicted ratings, and which product each customer prefers.

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{2.2}
\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Predicted Ratings} & \textbf{Customer 1} & \textbf{Customer 2} & \textbf{Customer 3} \\ \hline
Product 1 & 3 & 8 & 5 \\ \hline
Product 2 & 6 & 5 & 6 \\ \hline
Prefers & Product 2 & Product 1 & Product 2 \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
```

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{=html}
<table style="border-collapse: collapse; margin: 1em auto; text-align: center;">
<tr><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 8px 14px;">Predicted Ratings</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 8px 14px; width: 120px;">Customer 1</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 8px 14px; width: 120px;">Customer 2</th><th style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 8px 14px; width: 120px;">Customer 3</th></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 14px;">Product 1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">3</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">8</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">5</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 14px;">Product 2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">6</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">5</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">6</td></tr>
<tr><td style="border: 1px solid #000; padding: 14px;">Prefers</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">Product 2</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">Product 1</td><td style="border: 1px solid #000;">Product 2</td></tr>
</table>
```
:::

b) Find the overall preference (the average predicted rating over the 3 customers) for each product. Which product is preferred overall?

Product 1: $(3 + 8 + 5) \div 3 = 16 \div 3 \approx$ **5.33** \
Product 2: $(6 + 5 + 6) \div 3 = 17 \div 3 \approx$ **5.67** \
**Product 2 is preferred overall.** It has the higher average rating, and 2 of the 3 customers prefer it.

Choose the best answer for each question.

**2.** On DoltHub, why would you make changes to a database on a branch instead of directly on `main`?

A) So the data on `main` stays the same until you check your changes and merge them\
B) So the database gets new tables automatically\
C) So the changes can never be merged\
D) So other people can't see the database

**Answer: A** - Branches work the same way in DoltHub as in GitHub: `main` doesn't change until you merge.

**3.** In GitHub, you create a branch called `fix-header`, change `index.html` on that branch, and commit and push the change to your repository. What happens to `index.html` on `main`?

A) It has the same change\
B) It is deleted\
C) It stays the same; the change is only on `fix-header` until you merge it\
D) It is renamed to `fix-header`

**Answer: C** - A commit on a branch stays on that branch. `main` gets the change only when the branch is merged.

**4.** What is an AI agent, like OpenCode, Claude Code, or Codex?

A) A person who is a collaborator on the repository\
B) A GitHub setting for private repositories\
C) An AI helper that can edit files and run commands for you\
D) A type of database table

**Answer: C** - You describe a task and the agent works directly in your files.

**5.** On DoltHub, how do you save a query as a view?

A) Upload it as a file named `view.sql`\
B) Paste it into the database's README\
C) Copy and paste it into Gemini\
D) Run it in the SQL editor, then click **Create view** under the result and give the view a name

**Answer: D** - Name it with lowercase letters and underscores, like `customer_spending`.

**6.** Which of these is true about a primary key?

A) Two rows can share the same value\
B) Every row has a different value\
C) It must be a text column\
D) It is always the last column

**Answer: B** - Primary key values are unique: no two rows share one.

**7.** Why is a person's first name and last name not a good primary key?

A) Names are too long to store\
B) Two different people can have the same name, like two John Smiths\
C) Names have to be kept in a separate table\
D) A primary key can only be one letter

**Answer: B** - A primary key must be unique, and names are not. Names can also change.

**8.** In a database, what is a foreign key?

A) A column that refers to the primary key of another table\
B) A key from a database in another country\
C) A column that must be text\
D) A copy of the whole table

**Answer: A** - A foreign key connects a row in one table to a row in another.

**Questions 9 to 11 refer to this small database.** Order 6 has not been filled in yet.

**Customers**

| customer_id | first_name | last_name |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Jane | Smith |
| 3 | Robert | Johnson |
| 4 | Sarah | Williams |

**Products**

| product_id | name | price |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | Cashmere Sweater | 149.99 |
| 4 | Leather Jacket | 249.99 |
| 5 | Cotton T-Shirt | 29.99 |

**Orders**

| order_id | customer_id | product_id | order_date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 4 | 3 | 2025-03-20 |
| 5 | 3 | 4 | 2025-03-22 |
| 6 | ? | ? | 2025-03-25 |

**9.** Who placed order 5, and what did they buy?

A) Robert Johnson bought a Leather Jacket\
B) Sarah Williams bought a Cashmere Sweater\
C) Sarah Williams bought a Leather Jacket\
D) Robert Johnson bought a Cotton T-Shirt

**Answer: A** - Order 5 has `customer_id` 3 (Robert Johnson) and `product_id` 4 (Leather Jacket).

**10.** What was the price of the product bought in order 4?

A) 249.99\
B) 29.99\
C) 149.99\
D) You can't tell, because the Orders table has no price column

**Answer: C** - Order 4 has `product_id` 3. Looking up product 3 in Products gives the Cashmere Sweater at 149.99.

**11.** On 2025-03-25, Jane Smith buys a Cotton T-Shirt, and it is recorded as order 6. What goes in place of the two `?` marks for `customer_id` and `product_id`?

A) `customer_id` 5, `product_id` 2\
B) `customer_id` 2, `product_id` 5\
C) `customer_id` 2, `product_id` 3\
D) `customer_id` Jane Smith, `product_id` Cotton T-Shirt

**Answer: B** - Jane Smith is customer 2 and the Cotton T-Shirt is product 5.

**12.** In SQL, what does a `JOIN` do?

A) Deletes rows that two tables share\
B) Creates a new database\
C) Merges a branch into `main`\
D) Matches a foreign key in one table to the primary key in another, so their columns appear together

**Answer: D** - A JOIN uses the foreign key to line up matching rows, like each order with its customer's name.
